headline: US stocks closed higher as tech rebounded on pullback in 10-year yield from 2002-era highs ahead of September jobs report
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) rose 0.24% to 7,665.76, the Dow ($DJI) added about 0.10%, the Nasdaq ($COMP) and Nasdaq 100 ($NDX) gained roughly 0.36%, and the Russell 2000 (IWM) advanced 0.37% after a late rebound led by software and chip stocks.
- The 10-year Treasury yield spiked to 5.3445%, its highest level since 2002, before retreating from multi-decade highs, easing pressure on equities after earlier weighing on rate-sensitive real estate investment trusts and utilities and pushing 30-year mortgage rates to nearly 7.3%.
- Weekly initial jobless claims held at 197,000 for the week, the fourth straight weekly decline, while the four-week average rose to 200,000 and continuing claims fell to 1.701 million, reinforcing labor-market resilience even as manufacturing data highlighted sustained inflation pressures.
- Accenture (ACN) jumped about 17–17.4% after fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS of $3.29 beat the $3.18 consensus on revenue of $18.68 billion versus $18.03 billion expected, supported by record managed services bookings of $12.8 billion and upbeat fiscal 2027 guidance, lifting Cognizant (CTSH) roughly 7% on read-across.
- Synopsys (SNPS) climbed about 13–13.1% on a strong growth outlook and news of a licensing deal worth more than $1 billion with Amazon Web Services (AMZN) plus an AI-chip partnership with OpenAI (OAIW).
- Coherent (COHR) gained 10% after unveiling its PhotonLink optics platform for AI data centers and receiving a new Outperform rating from Bernstein.
- Micron (MU) ultimately joined the chip rally as investors digested earnings that beat estimates with nearly quadrupled revenue, roughly $32 billion in AI-related customer commitments, and a raised Q1 outlook following an initially mixed, near-flat reaction.
- Corteva (CTVA) plunged 84%, wiping out more than $42 billion in market value in a move tied to a major corporate action.
- After the close, Nike (NKE) reported quarterly results, while Anthropic (ANTW) advanced initial public offering plans targeting a mid-November listing.
- Investors looked ahead to tomorrow’s September employment report and several scheduled Federal Reserve speeches as the next key macro catalysts.
